title: Tesla Stock (TSLA) Falls 1.2% on EU Self-Driving Vote Delay (Nov 25)
summary: Tesla (TSLA) closed at $380.14 on Nov 25, down 1.18%, as the EU postponed a review of its assisted-driving system and SpaceX merger reports weighed.
body_markdown:
## Why Tesla Stock Fell


According to[International Business Times AU](https://www.ibtimes.com.au/tesla-shares-fall-eu-fsd-delay-spacex-merger-talks-1879380) , regulators reportedly postponed a meeting of the European Union's Technical Committee for Motor Vehicles on Tesla's assisted-driving system from December 1 to December 15, and a European Commission spokesperson confirmed the new date to Reuters. The outlet reported that two earlier meetings this year ended without a vote, that 12 EU countries have approved the technology so far, and that bloc-wide approval needs at least 15 of the 27 member states, representing 65% of the EU population.


The second factor was the SpaceX deal talk. As reported by[FinanceFeeds](https://financefeeds.com/tesla-and-spacex-shares-slide-as-merger-concerns-and-eu-approval-delay-mount/) , the declines followed reports that Tesla and SpaceX had appointed five directors and three investment banks for a[possible all-stock combination valued at about $3.5 trillion](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/spacex-tesla-merger-talks-3-5-trillion-deal/) , with Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs advising SpaceX and Evercore working with Tesla. FinanceFeeds noted that neither company has announced a definitive merger agreement, valuation terms or an exchange ratio, and described the declines as reflecting investor concerns amid a broader market sell-off.


Per[The Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/breakfast-news/2026/11/25/breakfast-news/?source=iedfolrf0000001) , the Financial Times reported the merger talks, and Elon Musk holds about 20% of Tesla's voting power but more than 80% of SpaceX's votes. The Motley Fool noted that Tesla holders will want a favorable exchange ratio.


## TSLA Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- Tesla closed $22.50 above its session low, recovering from its intraday low on volume 7.83% below average.
- National approvals are building, with 12 EU countries clearing the assisted-driving system and Italy approving it last week, according to International Business Times AU.
- The two companies already do business together: Tesla booked $626 million of Megapack battery revenue from SpaceX during the first nine months of 2026, per The Motley Fool.


### Risks


- A negative EU-level decision could invalidate existing national approvals, FinanceFeeds reported, and France and Sweden have raised safety and speeding concerns, per International Business Times AU.
- Merger terms remain undisclosed, and Tesla has said its independent committee must recommend any deal first, according to FinanceFeeds.
- Depending on the terms, Musk could end up with majority control of a combined company, The Motley Fool noted.


The next confirmed event is the December 15 EU committee meeting on Tesla's assisted-driving system.
